Summary: AE-BUG-001 - Authenticated user information remains visible after logout when navigating back
Description:
Related test case: AE-LOGOUT-001
Module: Logout
Defect type: Session / Navigation
Source severity: Medium
Source priority: High
Environment: Web application
Brave v193.129/Win11
URL: https://automationexercise.com
Preconditions: 1. Active registered test account exists.
2. User begins logged out.
Steps to reproduce: 1. Open Automation Exercise.
2. Click Signup / Login.
3. Enter valid registered credentials.
4. Click Login.
5. Confirm “Logged in as [username]” is displayed.
6. Click Logout.
7. Click the browser Back button.
8. Observe the page.
9. Refresh the page and attempt to open an authenticated feature to verify whether access persists.
Expected result: After logout, browser navigation should not display authenticated user information or provide access to authenticated functionality.
Actual result: After logout, clicking the browser Back button displayed the previous page with “Logged in as Kevin Tester” and the Logout option. Further verification is required to determine whether the page was cached or the authenticated session remained active.
Source defect status: Open
Reported by: KM
Date reported: 46232
Evidence / screenshot: ..\Screenshots\AE-LOGOUT-001.png
Retest status: Not Retested
QA notes: Potential cached page behavior. Confirm session state by refreshing and accessing a protected feature before final severity assessment.

Summary: AE-BUG-004 - The quantity field on the product-detail page does not respond when the user attempts to edit it. As a result, the user cannot select the desired quantity before adding the product to the cart.
Description:
Related test case: AE-CART-002
Module: Cart
Defect type: Functional / User Interface
Source severity: High
Source priority: High
Environment: Web application
Brave v193.129/Win11
Preconditions: 1. Website is available
2. User is logged out
3. At least two products are available
Steps to reproduce: 1. Open https://automationexercise.com while logged out.
2. Click View Product for any available product.
3. Add product to Cart
4. View Cart
5. Click inside the quantity field.
6. Attempt to change the quantity from 1 to 4.
Expected result: The quantity field should accept a valid quantity of 4. After the product is added, the cart should display the selected product with a quantity of 4 and a line total equal to the unit price multiplied by 4
Actual result: The populated cart page is displayed, but the quantity field cannot be edited. Clicking the field produces no response, preventing the user from selecting a quantity of 4.
Source defect status: Rejected
Reported by: KM
Date reported: 46234
Evidence / screenshot: ..\Automation\Execution Evidence\AE-CART-002.png
Assigned to: N/A
Resolution / developer notes: Initial execution attempted to edit the quantity in the cart. The documented scenario requires setting the quantity on the product-detail page before adding the product to the cart. Manual retest and corrected Playwright automation confirmed quantity 4 and the correct line total.
Retest status: Pass
Retest date: 46240
QA notes: Rejected as not an application defect. The original failure resulted from using the wrong interaction point.
